the saturation model provides the most successful description of DIS off nuclei in the whole kinematic range of the HERA experiments.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear attenuation is a universal phenomenon in the saturation regime, where the partons in the nuclei become strongly interacting.
the nuclear WW gluon is the key to understanding the saturation and diffractive phenomena in DIS off nuclei.
the WW glue is the only object which is needed for the description of the nuclear attenuation of the photon and gluon structure function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nuclear WW glue is a universal object that is the same in DIS and the Drell-Yan process, and that it is the same as the nuclear parton distribution function (nPDF) in the limit of small Bjorken $x$.
the nuclear WW gluon is the natural generalization of the nuclear PDF to the regime of high gluon densities.
